african-documentary.title: AFRICAN DOCUMENTARY
african-documentary.intro: Working for over two decades commissioned as a documentary photographer with various local and international aid agencies has revealed in intimate detail the heart of who we are as a people across Africa. Engaging with communities living on the threshold of human existence reveals the very essence of our ‘human condition’. How do we not only survive in the 21 century but importantly how do we create opportunities to thrive and empower ourselves by harnessing modern technology, realizing food and water security, gain access to primary health care and perhaps the most important aspect, how do we embolden communities to break the cycle of corruption, poverty and apathy. The heart of my visual documentation is the power of visual story-telling, creating a strong narrative so as to bridge the divides.

african-pangolin.title: African Pangolin
african-pangolin.intro: This very rare collection of a wild Pangolin photographed out in the wild savannah of northern Kwa Zulu-Natal having carried a makeshift studio around for six hours finally paid off. There is no human interaction when tracking or engaging with the wild pangolin. Of its own free will it made its way onto the screen. Halfway across this magnificent animal stopped and enjoyed a tumble around on this strange new surface. Rare.

an-african-portrait.title: AFRICAN PORTRAIT
an-african-portrait.intro: I have worked for over 20 years across Southern & East Africa photographing for some of the worlds foremost organisations & institutions committed to the upliftment, development and progress of marginalized, impoverished and disenfranchised communities. Issues tackled include food security, water security, primary healthcare, HIV & Aids, Malaria, TB and education.

an-afternoon-in-havana.title: AN AFTERNOON IN HAVANA
an-afternoon-in-havana.intro: The hearts of boys are wild and free, they throw caution to the wind with every chance encounter. Nothing is off-limits and everything an adventure. I have a deep longing to connect with moments that are spontaneous and unplanned. My invading the space of these youthful boys congregating along the Malecon at the harbour entrance to Havana was an extraordinary moment of pure joy and energy. Every wolf pack have their centuries that lookout for possible danger. These boys were constantly watching for any approaching police or authority. In a communist country where ‘Big Brother’ watches over you where even the ice cream shops are nationalised, freedom is sought at every opportunity. This collection recorded in only a few minutes speaks of the resilience of youth, a group of boys who one day will face many bigger challenges. If only for a moment one late Summers afternoon life was beautiful and free.

art-of-mw.title: Shape of Light
art-of-mw.intro: An ongoing exploratory collection inspired by the photographer’s desire & passion to create images of sheer imagination. An opportunity for models to express themselves as if nobody was watching. This body of work is an opportunity to feel free, to concoct an idea and to have it come to life in front of the lens is a privilege all of its own. It is within these moments whilst capturing the ‘decisive moment’ that I feel most alive with my work.

black.title: BLACK
black.intro: An exploratory collection, a work in progress

boys-of-the-royal-ballet.title: BOYS OF THE ROYAL BALLET
boys-of-the-royal-ballet.intro: Some shoots last minutes whilst others take years. The privilege to work with the Royal Ballet School across the lower and upper houses of the Royal Ballet School was an achievement that took approximately 8 years to complete. Sometimes it was finances other times it was a refusal to enter in. Yet like with many collections I create, many are started and over years they slowly find a conclusion. This collection is a deeply moving and an emotional body of work for me. Having danced ballet for 20 years, knowing what these young boys and men are going through became a very personal journey.

deep-level-mining-south-africa.title: DEEP LEVEL MINING SOUTH AFRICA
deep-level-mining-south-africa.intro: The history of underground mining in South Africa is rooted and intertwined in the legacy of a mighty migrant labour force traveling to the Vaal Reefs from all corners of Southern Africa to earn meagre salaries to take home to their communities and villages. Following in the footsteps of legendary South African photographers, Willman journeyed deep within the bowls of our African soil to discover for himself one of Southern Africa’s greatest legacies.

famous-faces.title: FAMOUS FACES
famous-faces.intro: “The general illusion is that there is no self-awareness where in contrast it’s all about self-awareness, who we are and what we shaped ourselves to be….” Matthew Willman speaking to an audience in Hong Kong regarding the personalities he has photographed.

our-mandela.title: MANDELA: A portrait of an African icon
our-mandela.intro: Between 2003 - 2013 I was commissioned with the Nelson Mandela Foundation in Johannesburg to contribute to the building of the Nelson Mandela Centre of Memory archives as a photographer. Between 2001 and 2023 I have actively documented an extraordinary body of work on the life of Nelson Mandela. ‘Our Mandela’ narrates this extraordinary journey through an exhibition rich in photographic detail and dogged determination.

out-the-ordinary.title: OUT THE ORDINARY
out-the-ordinary.intro: Having lived my whole life through the eye of a camera. I tend to exist in a world through the interpretation of what is real and that which is complete imagination. The images are a revelation, not only of this imagination but also a window into worlds, created by people and places I ventured out to discover. Somehow, they too, are a reflection of myself. The art of photography is in allowing the ordinary to become the extraordinary.

private-space.title: PRIVATE SPACE
private-space.intro: ‘Private Space’ is a visual masterpiece, an incredible journey not only as a photographer but also as a former dancer himself. The collection took 5 years to produce working with 88 dancers from 42 countries on 5 continents. There is a relationship between a dancer and a photographer. The two it seems are married to each other not by the means with which they achieve their greatness, but rather by their passion that creates the magic. No great photographer was without their camera, yet no one will say the photographers’ talent lay with the camera. No great dancer was without their stage, yet no one ever said a dancer’s greatness was because of the stage. It’s not about the stage and it’s not about the camera. The art lies solely with the creativity and imagination of these two artists. Both with years of training and experience who if for only a few moments have the power to move the audience into a space that is somewhere between reality and the dream. ‘Private Space’ is a visual masterpiece an ode to ballet. A personal journey of a photographer with his dancers. Every image is an intimate moment, a private love affair expressed by dancers from around the world.

studio.title: STUDIO
studio.intro: Richard Avedon spoke truth when referencing dance and photography, ‘The two it seems are married to each other.’

the-inanda-heritage.title: INANDA HERITAGE
the-inanda-heritage.intro: The Inanda Heritage Collection marks the very first photographic documentary collection of Matthew Willman in 2000 / 2001. Over a period of 3 months Willman went out on his own to photograph the people of the Inanda Valley. Steeped in history, the Inanda Valley is considered to be the birthplace of democracy in South Africa. Mahatma Gandhi created his passive resistance policies whilst living in the Inanda at the turn of the 20th century. Mandela voted in 1994 in the Inanda Valley. The valley is home to one of the most diverse cultural, religious and traditional communities in Southern Africa due in part to the port city of Durban. Yet for almost every white family living in their small suburbs alongside the Inanda, they remain oblivious to this incredible location on their doorstep. As a young South African growing up during the last years of Apartheid I was desperate to get involved, to learn and to become a part of the change that was happening in South Africa. The camera afforded me the opportunity to step into these African rural and township communities. Understanding exists on the other side of fear. It was from this first collection that Willman went on to dedicate the majority of his career over the next 20 years to humanitarian causes alongside international organisations across Southern & East Africa.

the-robben-island-story.title: ROBBEN ISLAND
the-robben-island-story.intro: In 2004 Nelson Mandela launched the Mandela Centre of Memory which today houses the archive of Nelson Mandela’s life. 3 Months prior to the launch of the archive library, Mr Mandela along with the Nelson Mandela Foundation chose 18 of my works from out my Robben Island Collection to celebrate the official opening. In 2001 armed with only a camera and rolls of 24 exposure black and white film, Willman began documenting Robben Island independently. After much harassment by The Robben Island Museum it was finally agreed upon that Willman could complete his documentary. 18 months later the collection was complete. It was this body of work that gained the attention of not only the Nelson Mandela Foundation but various other institutions around the world. The Robben Island Collection has exhibited around the world with many of the works forming part of permanent collections in International museums.
